title: StablecoinBridge enforces its mint limit on raw source-token balance, not on ZCHF minted, so donated XCHF permanently consumes mint capacity
description:
Coupled Pair: chf.balanceOf(bridge) ↔ ZCHF minted through the bridge
Breaking Operation: direct chf.transfer(bridge, x) (no bridge function runs)
Masking Code: require(chf.balanceOf(address(this)) <= limit)
The bridge has no minted counter; it infers outstanding ZCHF from its XCHF balance. XCHF sent straight to the bridge raises the balance without any ZCHF being minted, so the limit check then rejects legitimate mints.
root_cause: Invariant: XCHF held == ZCHF minted by the bridge (minus burned). A plain token transfer into the bridge breaks it, and the limit check trusts the balance. The surplus XCHF can only leave via ZCHF burns, so the capacity is lost until holders burn.

harm.loses_what: availability of mint capacity (DoS up to limit)
harm.magnitude: attacker must donate up to limit minus current balance in XCHF, recoverable only by ZCHF burners

exploit_trace: 2. Attacker transfers L-B XCHF directly to the bridge.
3. Any mint(amount>0) now fails the limit check; no ZCHF backs the donated XCHF.
4. Capacity returns only as ZCHF holders burn and withdraw the donated XCHF.

preconditions.text: attacker holds XCHF equal to the remaining limit

title: Equity voteAnchor doubles as holding-duration clock, so anyone can reset a holder's redeem eligibility by sending them freshly acquired FPS
description:
Coupled Pair: balanceOf[holder] ↔ voteAnchor[holder] (holding duration used by canRedeem)
Breaking Operation: _beforeTokenTransfer() on an inbound transfer from a third party
The recipient's anchor is moved to the balance-weighted average on every inbound transfer, with no consent from the recipient. canRedeem() reads the same anchor to enforce the 90-day minimum holding, so unsolicited transfers shorten a victim's average holding time.
root_cause: Invariant: a holder's average holding age reflects only shares they chose to acquire. The anchor is updated for any incoming transfer, so a third party can drive anchorTime - voteAnchor below MIN_HOLDING_DURATION and block redeem() until the new average ages.

harm.loses_what: ability to redeem for up to ~90 days
harm.magnitude: attacker must give away the transferred FPS; a holder only slightly past the threshold needs little

exploit_trace: 1. Victim holds B FPS with average age just above 90 days.
2. Attacker sends x freshly acquired FPS to victim.
3. Victim anchor moves to age*B/(B+x) < 90 days.
4. canRedeem(victim) is false and redeem() reverts until the average ages again.

preconditions.text: victim average holding age close to or above threshold
